# Diagnostic codes

<!-- Generated by tests/docs.test.ts from tests/support/checks-doc.ts and the
     fixtures in tests/fixtures/errors/. Do not edit by hand; regenerate with
     UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm test. -->

Every problem `tejun check` reports has a code, the exact place in the source,
a help line, and the message in Japanese. Syntax errors stop at the first one;
every other check reports all problems at once. Each example below is the real
output for a broken file in `tests/fixtures/errors/`.

- **T02xx Safety: timeouts, reachability, handlers, interlocks:** [T0201](#t0201) [T0202](#t0202) [T0203](#t0203) [T0204](#t0204) [T0205](#t0205) [T0206](#t0206) [T0207](#t0207) [T0208](#t0208) [T0209](#t0209) [T0210](#t0210)
- **T03xx I/O:** [T0301](#t0301) [T0302](#t0302) [T0303](#t0303) [T0304](#t0304) [T0305](#t0305) [T0306](#t0306)

## T00xx: Syntax

### T0001

**unexpected character.** A character that cannot start any token. Common causes: full-width punctuation typed with a Japanese IME (`；`, `（`), Japanese text outside a string or comment, `=` instead of `==`.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0001_fullwidth_semicolon.tejun`:

```text
error[T0001]: unexpected character `；`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0001_fullwidth_semicolon.tejun:12:29
   |
12 |     state Idle { conveyor on； when part_present forever -> Run }
   |                             ^^ not allowed here
   |
   = help: this is a full-width `；`; use the ASCII `;`
   = 日本語: 予期しない文字 `；`
```

**Fix:** Use the ASCII character the hint names, or move the text into a `"string"` or `// comment`.

### T0002

**unterminated string.** A string that is not closed before the end of the line. Strings cannot span lines.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0002_unterminated_string.tejun`:

```text
error[T0002]: unterminated string
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0002_unterminated_string.tejun:4:45
  |
4 |     input  part_present : bool     @ %IX0.0 "ワーク検出
  |                                             ^^^^^^^^^^^ this string is never closed
  |
  = help: add a closing `"` before the end of the line
  = 日本語: 文字列が閉じられていません
```

**Fix:** Add the closing `"`.

### T0003

**malformed I/O address.** A malformed I/O address, such as `%QX9` (no bit number), `%QX0.8` (bit above 7) or `%MX0.0` (memory area). Wrong addresses are a classic way to drive the wrong actuator.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0003_address_missing_bit.tejun`:

```text
error[T0003]: malformed I/O address `%QX9`
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0003_address_missing_bit.tejun:7:38
  |
7 |     output conveyor     : bool     @ %QX9 "コンベア"
  |                                      ^^^^ not a valid address
  |
  = help: a bit address needs a byte and a bit number, like %QX0.1
  = 日本語: 不正なI/Oアドレス `%QX9`
```

**Fix:** Write `%IX<byte>.<bit>` / `%QX<byte>.<bit>` with a bit from 0 to 7, or `%IW<n>` / `%QW<n>`. For a bit above 7 the hint gives the next byte.

### T0010

**unexpected token.** The parser expected one thing and found another, such as a missing `:` in an I/O line or a wrong handler body.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0010_handler_body.tejun`:

```text
error[T0010]: expected `safe`, found name `off`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0010_handler_body.tejun:15:29
   |
15 |   on not estop_ok { outputs off; -> Stopped }
   |                             ^^^ expected `safe`
   |
   = help: a handler body is `outputs safe; -> Stopped`
   = 日本語: `safe` が必要ですが、名前 `off` が見つかりました
```

**Fix:** Write what the message says is expected; the help line shows the full form of the construct.

### T0011

**unclosed brace at end of file.** The file ends while a `{` is still open. The caret points at the `{` that was never closed.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0011_unclosed_brace.tejun`:

```text
error[T0011]: unexpected end of file: `{` is never closed
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0011_unclosed_brace.tejun:2:19
  |
2 | station Demo "デモ" {
  |                     ^ this `{` is never closed
  |
  = help: add the matching `}`
  = 日本語: ファイルが途中で終わっています: `{` が閉じられていません
```

**Fix:** Add the matching `}`.

### T0012

**unknown keyword.** A word where a keyword belongs, usually a typo such as `interlok` or `wen`.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0012_misspelled_when.tejun`:

```text
error[T0012]: unknown keyword `wen`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0012_misspelled_when.tejun:12:31
   |
12 |     state Idle { conveyor on; wen part_present forever -> Run }
   |                               ^^^ unknown keyword
   |
   = help: did you mean `when`?
   = 日本語: 不明なキーワード `wen`
```

**Fix:** Use the keyword suggested by `did you mean`.

### T0013

**keyword used as a name.** A reserved keyword used as a name, e.g. a signal called `state`.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0013_keyword_as_name.tejun`:

```text
error[T0013]: `state` is a keyword and cannot be used as a name
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0013_keyword_as_name.tejun:7:12
  |
7 |     output state        : bool     @ %QX0.0 "コンベア"
  |            ^^^^^ expected a signal name
  |
  = help: choose another name, such as `state_1`
  = 日本語: `state` はキーワードのため名前として使えません
```

**Fix:** Choose another name.

### T0014

**section out of order or repeated.** A station section out of order, or repeated. The order is fixed so every station reads the same way.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0014_section_order.tejun`:

```text
error[T0014]: `interlock` must come before `sequence`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0014_section_order.tejun:14:3
   |
14 |   interlock press_force < 40 kN else fault OVERLOAD
   |   ^^^^^^^^^ out of order
   |
   = help: sections go in this order: io, device, interlock, sequence, on
   = 日本語: `interlock` は `sequence` より前に書く必要があります
```

**Fix:** Order the sections `io`, `device`, `interlock`, `sequence`, `on`, with one `io` and one `sequence`.

### T0015

**chained comparison.** A chained comparison such as `0 < x < 40`, which does not mean what it looks like in most languages.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0015_chained_comparison.tejun`:

```text
error[T0015]: comparisons cannot be chained
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0015_chained_comparison.tejun:10:13
   |
10 |   interlock 0 kN < press_force < 40 kN else fault OVERLOAD
   |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ chained comparison
   |
   = help: compare each pair and join them with `and`, e.g. `0 < x and x < 40`
   = 日本語: 比較演算子は連結できません
```

**Fix:** Compare each pair and join them: `0 < x and x < 40`.

### T0016

**missing `;` between statements.** Two statements in a state with no `;` between them.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0016_missing_semicolon.tejun`:

```text
error[T0016]: missing `;` between statements
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0016_missing_semicolon.tejun:12:29
   |
12 |     state Idle { conveyor on when part_present forever -> Run }
   |                             ^ expected `;` here
   |
   = help: separate statements in a state with `;`
   = 日本語: 文の間に `;` がありません
```

**Fix:** Separate statements with `;`.

## T01xx: Names, types and units

### T0101

**undefined name.** A signal, device or state that is used but never declared.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0101_undefined_signal.tejun`:

```text
error[T0101]: undefined name `part_presnt`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0101_undefined_signal.tejun:18:39
   |
18 |     state Idle    { conveyor on; when part_presnt forever -> Clamp }
   |                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^ not declared
   |
   = help: did you mean `part_present`?
   = 日本語: 未定義の名前 `part_presnt`
```

**Fix:** Fix the spelling (see `did you mean`), or declare it.

### T0102

**duplicate name.** The same name declared twice, a state named `Stopped`, or a fault named `POSITION_MISMATCH` or `FEEDBACK_MISMATCH`. These are built in: handlers go to `Stopped`, and the device check raises `POSITION_MISMATCH` (Cylinder) and `FEEDBACK_MISMATCH` (Motor).

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0102_builtin_stopped.tejun`:

```text
error[T0102]: `Stopped` is a built-in state and cannot be declared
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0102_builtin_stopped.tejun:22:11
   |
22 |     state Stopped { -> Idle }
   |           ^^^^^^^ built-in state
   |
   = help: handlers go to `Stopped` automatically; choose another name for this state
   = 日本語: `Stopped` は組み込みの状態のため宣言できません
```

**Fix:** Rename one of them. Never declare `Stopped` or raise a built-in device fault yourself.

### T0103

**type mismatch.** A value of the wrong type: a real signal used as a condition, a bool compared with `<`, a device used as a signal, a real output switched on.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0103_bool_compared.tejun`:

```text
error[T0103]: `<` compares numbers, but `part_present` is bool
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0103_bool_compared.tejun:16:13
   |
16 |   interlock part_present < 40 kN else fault OVERLOAD
   |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ bool in a numeric comparison
   |
   = help: use a bool signal directly as a condition: `part_present` or `not part_present`
   = 日本語: `<` は数値を比較しますが、`part_present` は bool です
```

**Fix:** Compare reals with a limit (`press_force < 40 kN`); use bools directly; use a device state like `clamp.retracted`.

### T0104

**unit mismatch.** A comparison whose sides have different units, or a number without a unit compared with a signal that has one. Tejun never converts units silently.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0104_missing_unit.tejun`:

```text
error[T0104]: `40` has no unit, but `press_force` is in kN
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0104_missing_unit.tejun:16:27
   |
16 |   interlock press_force < 40 else fault OVERLOAD
   |                           ^^ missing unit
   |
   = help: write `40 kN`
   = 日本語: `40` に単位がありませんが、`press_force` は kN です
```

**Fix:** Write the number in the signal's unit; for convertible units the help line gives the converted value (`40 N` → `0.04 kN`).

### T0105

**unknown unit.** A unit Tejun does not know, such as `msec` or `kn` (units are case-sensitive).

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0105_unknown_unit.tejun`:

```text
error[T0105]: unknown unit `msec`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0105_unknown_unit.tejun:20:31
   |
20 |     state Press   { hold 1500 msec; -> Release }
   |                               ^^^^ unknown unit
   |
   = help: did you mean `ms`?
   = 日本語: 不明な単位 `msec`
```

**Fix:** Use a known unit: `N kN mm m bar kPa MPa degC rpm A V`, and `ms` or `s` for times.

### T0106

**value outside the declared range.** A comparison that can never change result over the signal's declared range (e.g. `press_force < 60 kN` with range 0..50 is always true), so it protects nothing; or an empty range.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0106_outside_range.tejun`:

```text
error[T0106]: `press_force < 60 kN` is always true: `press_force` is declared as 0..50 kN
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0106_outside_range.tejun:16:27
   |
16 |   interlock press_force < 60 kN else fault OVERLOAD
   |                           ^^^^^ outside 0..50
   |
   = help: check the limit; a comparison that never changes protects nothing
   = 日本語: `press_force < 60 kN` は常に真です: `press_force` の範囲は 0..50 kN です
```

**Fix:** Use a limit inside the range, or correct the range.

### T0107

**name not usable in Structured Text.** A name that would break the generated Structured Text: an ST reserved word (`step`, `time`, `do`…), a name starting with `tj_` (reserved for generated code), or two names that differ only in case (ST ignores case).

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0107_st_reserved_word.tejun`:

```text
error[T0107]: `step` is a reserved word in Structured Text
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0107_st_reserved_word.tejun:4:12
  |
4 |     input  step : bool     @ %IX0.0 "ワーク検出"
  |            ^^^^ reserved in Structured Text
  |
  = help: the generated PLC code would not compile; rename it, e.g. `step_sig`
  = 日本語: `step` は Structured Text の予約語です
```

**Fix:** Rename it.

## T02xx: Safety: timeouts, reachability, handlers, interlocks

### T0201

**wait with no timeout.** A wait with no timeout: a device action, or a `when` that can wait. If a sensor fails, the machine would wait forever without raising a fault.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0201_device_action_no_timeout.tejun`:

```text
error[T0201]: `clamp.extend` can wait forever: it has no timeout
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0201_device_action_no_timeout.tejun:19:21
   |
19 |     state Clamp   { clamp.extend; -> Press }
   |                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^ no timeout
   |
   = help: add `within <time> else fault <CODE>`, or `forever` if waiting forever is intended
   = 日本語: `clamp.extend` にタイムアウトがないため、永久に待つ可能性があります
```

**Fix:** Add `within <time> else fault <CODE>`, or write `forever` when waiting forever is intended (e.g. waiting for the next part).

### T0202

**unreachable state.** A state that no transition leads to from the first state. Unreachable logic is dead code that hides mistakes.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0202_unreachable_state.tejun`:

```text
error[T0202]: state `Spare` can never be reached
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0202_unreachable_state.tejun:22:11
   |
22 |     state Spare   { -> Idle }
   |           ^^^^^ unreachable
   |
   = help: no transition leads here from the start state `Idle`
   = 日本語: 状態 `Spare` に到達できません
```

**Fix:** Add a transition to it, or remove it.

### T0203

**interlock violated.** An interlock can be violated. The proof explores every reachable state with every combination of inputs and shows the shortest path. A common case: a device position is unknown at startup, or a device is still moving.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0203_conveyor_while_moving.tejun`:

```text
error[T0203]: interlock violated: `conveyor` can be ON while `clamp.retracted` is false
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0203_conveyor_while_moving.tejun:23:21
   |
23 |     state Release { conveyor on; clamp.retract within 2 s else fault RELEASE_TIMEOUT; -> Idle }
   |                     ^^^^^^^^^^^ `conveyor` is ON here in `Release`
   |
   = path: Home -> Idle -> Clamp -> Press -> Release
   = interlock: `interlock conveyor requires clamp.retracted` (line 16)
   = help: `clamp` is still moving in `Release`; switch `conveyor` on only after the move is confirmed
   = 日本語: インターロック違反: `clamp.retracted` が偽のときに `conveyor` がONになる可能性があります
```

**Fix:** Follow the help line: home the device first (`state Home { clamp.retract … -> Idle }`), switch the output on only after the move is confirmed, or switch one of the outputs off in that state.

### T0204

**fault with no `on fault` handler.** A fault can be raised but nothing handles it. Every station with a device can fault: the built-in device check raises `POSITION_MISMATCH` (Cylinder) or `FEEDBACK_MISMATCH` (Motor) when a device's sensors disagree with its tracked state.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0204_no_fault_handler.tejun`:

```text
error[T0204]: fault `OVERLOAD` can be raised, but there is no `on fault` handler
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0204_no_fault_handler.tejun:16:44
   |
16 |   interlock press_force < 40 kN else fault OVERLOAD
   |                                            ^^^^^^^^ nowhere to go
   |
   = help: add `on fault { outputs safe; -> Stopped }` at the end of the station
   = 日本語: 故障 `OVERLOAD` が発生する可能性がありますが、`on fault` ハンドラがありません
```

**Fix:** Add `on fault { outputs safe; -> Stopped }`.

### T0205

**no E-stop handler.** The station has no E-stop handler, or its E-stop input is not marked `safety`.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0205_no_estop_handler.tejun`:

```text
error[T0205]: station `Demo` has no E-stop handler
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0205_no_estop_handler.tejun:2:9
  |
2 | station Demo "デモ" {
  |         ^^^^ no E-stop handler
  |
  = help: add `on not estop_ok { outputs safe; -> Stopped }`
  = 日本語: ステーション `Demo` に非常停止ハンドラがありません
```

**Fix:** Declare the E-stop input with `safety` and add `on not estop_ok { outputs safe; -> Stopped }`.

### T0206

**dead-end state.** A state with no transition out. The machine would stay there until a fault or E-stop.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0206_dead_end_state.tejun`:

```text
error[T0206]: state `Release` has no way out
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0206_dead_end_state.tejun:21:11
   |
21 |     state Release { clamp.retract within 2 s else fault RELEASE_TIMEOUT }
   |           ^^^^^^^ dead end
   |
   = help: add a transition, e.g. `-> Idle`; otherwise only a fault or E-stop can leave this state
   = 日本語: 状態 `Release` から抜け出す遷移がありません
```

**Fix:** Add a transition, e.g. back to the idle state.

### T0207

**statement after a transition.** A statement after the state's transitions, or after a bare `-> State` where it can never run.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0207_after_transition.tejun`:

```text
error[T0207]: `conveyor on` comes after a transition
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0207_after_transition.tejun:18:57
   |
18 |     state Idle    { when part_present forever -> Clamp; conveyor on }
   |                                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^ after a transition
   |
   = help: write outputs and the step first, then the transitions
   = 日本語: `conveyor on` が遷移の後に書かれています
```

**Fix:** Write outputs and the step first, then the transitions; a bare `-> State` comes last.

### T0208

**more than one step in a state.** Two steps (device actions or `hold`s) in one state. A state waits for one thing at a time, which keeps timeouts and faults unambiguous.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0208_two_steps.tejun`:

```text
error[T0208]: state `Press` has more than one step
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0208_two_steps.tejun:20:35
   |
20 |     state Press   { hold 1500 ms; hold 500 ms; -> Release }
   |                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^ second step
   |
   = help: a state waits for one thing at a time; move `hold 500 ms` into its own state
   = 日本語: 状態 `Press` に複数のステップがあります
```

**Fix:** Move the second step into its own state.

### T0209

**handler does not go to `Stopped`.** A fault or E-stop handler that goes somewhere other than `Stopped`, e.g. restarting at `Idle`.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0209_handler_target.tejun`:

```text
error[T0209]: handler goes to `Idle` instead of `Stopped`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0209_handler_target.tejun:23:38
   |
23 |   on fault        { outputs safe; -> Idle }
   |                                      ^^^^ should be `Stopped`
   |
   = help: fault and E-stop handlers must stop the machine with `-> Stopped`; restarting is a separate, deliberate step
   = 日本語: ハンドラが `Stopped` ではなく `Idle` に遷移しています
```

**Fix:** End handlers with `-> Stopped`. Restarting after a fault is a separate, deliberate step.

### T0210

**station too large to prove.** The station has more than 10 free inputs to explore, too many for the interlock proof to finish quickly.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0210_too_many_inputs.tejun`:

```text
error[T0210]: station `Big` has 12 inputs to explore; the interlock proof handles at most 10
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0210_too_many_inputs.tejun:2:9
  |
2 | station Big "大きすぎる" {
  |         ^^^ too many inputs
  |
  = inputs: estop_ok, s0, s1, s2, s3, s4, s5, s6, s7, s8, s9, s10
  = help: split the machine into smaller stations, each with its own sequence
  = 日本語: ステーション `Big` には探索する入力が 12 個あります。インターロック証明は最大 10 個までです
```

**Fix:** Split the machine into smaller stations.

## T03xx: I/O

### T0301

**two signals on one address.** Two signals on the same address.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0301_duplicate_address.tejun`:

```text
error[T0301]: address `%QX0.1` is already used by `clamp_in`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0301_duplicate_address.tejun:11:38
   |
11 |     output conveyor     : bool     @ %QX0.1 "コンベア"
   |                                      ^^^^^^ used twice
   |
   = help: `clamp_in` is declared on line 10; give each signal its own address
   = 日本語: アドレス `%QX0.1` はすでに `clamp_in` が使用しています
```

**Fix:** Give each signal its own address.

### T0302

**address does not match the signal direction.** An input on an output address (`%Q…`) or an output on an input address (`%I…`).

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0302_input_on_output_address.tejun`:

```text
error[T0302]: input `part_present` is on output address `%QX0.3`
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0302_input_on_output_address.tejun:4:38
  |
4 |     input  part_present : bool     @ %QX0.3 "ワーク検出"
  |                                      ^^^^^^ output address
  |
  = help: inputs use %I addresses and outputs use %Q addresses
  = 日本語: 入力 `part_present` が出力アドレス `%QX0.3` に割り当てられています
```

**Fix:** Inputs use `%I`, outputs use `%Q`.

### T0303

**address does not match the signal type.** A bool on a word address or a real on a bit address.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0303_real_on_bit_address.tejun`:

```text
error[T0303]: real signal `press_force` is on a bit address `%IX1.0`
 --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0303_real_on_bit_address.tejun:8:38
  |
8 |     input  press_force  : real<kN> @ %IX1.0 "プレス荷重" range 0..50
  |                                      ^^^^^^ bit address
  |
  = help: bool signals use bit addresses like %IX0.0; real signals use word addresses like %IW2
  = 日本語: real 型の信号 `press_force` がビットアドレス `%IX1.0` に割り当てられています
```

**Fix:** Bools use bit addresses (`%IX0.0`), reals use word addresses (`%IW2`).

### T0304

**input used as an output.** An input switched on, or limited with `requires`. Inputs come from sensors; only outputs can be driven.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0304_input_switched_on.tejun`:

```text
error[T0304]: `part_present` is an input and cannot be switched on
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0304_input_switched_on.tejun:18:21
   |
18 |     state Idle    { part_present on; when part_present forever -> Clamp }
   |                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^ input
   |
   = help: only outputs can be switched on; inputs are read from sensors
   = 日本語: `part_present` は入力のためONにできません
```

**Fix:** Switch an output instead. For conditions on inputs use `interlock never (…)` or `<cond> else fault`.

### T0305

**safety signal used in sequence logic.** A safety input (E-stop, guard) used in sequence logic. The stop path must stay independent of the sequence.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0305_safety_in_sequence.tejun`:

```text
error[T0305]: safety signal `estop_ok` is used in sequence logic
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0305_safety_in_sequence.tejun:18:56
   |
18 |     state Idle    { conveyor on; when part_present and estop_ok forever -> Clamp }
   |                                                        ^^^^^^^^ safety signal
   |
   = help: keep the stop path independent of the sequence: handle it in `on not estop_ok { outputs safe; -> Stopped }`
   = 日本語: 安全信号 `estop_ok` がシーケンスのロジックで使われています
```

**Fix:** Handle it only in `on not estop_ok { … }` and interlocks.

### T0306

**`safety` on a signal that cannot be a safety input.** `safety` on an output or a real input.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0306_safety_on_output.tejun`:

```text
error[T0306]: `safety` applies only to bool inputs, but `conveyor` is an output
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0306_safety_on_output.tejun:11:52
   |
11 |     output conveyor     : bool     @ %QX0.2 "コンベア" safety
   |                                                        ^^^^^^ not allowed here
   |
   = help: mark E-stop and guard-door inputs as `safety`; outputs are made safe by `outputs safe` in handlers
   = 日本語: `safety` は bool 型の入力にのみ指定できますが、`conveyor` は出力です
```

**Fix:** Mark only bool inputs such as E-stop or guard switches as `safety`.

## T04xx: Devices

### T0401

**unknown device kind.** A device kind Tejun does not know, usually a typo.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0401_unknown_device_kind.tejun`:

```text
error[T0401]: unknown device kind `Cilinder`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0401_unknown_device_kind.tejun:13:18
   |
13 |   device clamp : Cilinder(extend: clamp_out, retract: clamp_in,
   |                  ^^^^^^^^ unknown device kind
   |
   = help: did you mean `Cylinder`?
   = 日本語: 不明なデバイス種別 `Cilinder`
```

**Fix:** Use `Cylinder` (the only device kind for now).

### T0402

**missing device parameter.** A device with a parameter missing, typically a feedback sensor. Without it Tejun cannot confirm that a move finished.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0402_missing_sensor.tejun`:

```text
error[T0402]: device `clamp` is missing parameter `at_ret`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0402_missing_sensor.tejun:13:10
   |
13 |   device clamp : Cylinder(extend: clamp_out, retract: clamp_in,
   |          ^^^^^ missing `at_ret`
   |
   = help: `at_ret` is the sensor that confirms the cylinder is retracted; without it Tejun cannot confirm the device's state
   = 日本語: デバイス `clamp` にパラメータ `at_ret` がありません
```

**Fix:** Wire every parameter: `extend`, `retract`, `at_ext`, `at_ret`.

### T0403

**unknown or repeated device parameter.** A device parameter that does not exist, or one given twice.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0403_unknown_parameter.tejun`:

```text
error[T0403]: Cylinder has no parameter `at_extnd`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0403_unknown_parameter.tejun:14:27
   |
14 |                           at_extnd: clamp_ext_ls, at_ret: clamp_ret_ls)
   |                           ^^^^^^^^ unknown parameter
   |
   = help: did you mean `at_ext`?
   = 日本語: Cylinder にパラメータ `at_extnd` はありません
```

**Fix:** Use the suggested parameter name; give each parameter once.

### T0404

**device parameter wired to the wrong kind of signal.** A device parameter wired to the wrong kind of signal, e.g. a sensor parameter wired to an output.

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0404_sensor_wired_to_output.tejun`:

```text
error[T0404]: parameter `at_ext` needs a bool input, but `conveyor` is an output
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0404_sensor_wired_to_output.tejun:14:35
   |
14 |                           at_ext: conveyor, at_ret: clamp_ret_ls)
   |                                   ^^^^^^^^ expected a bool input
   |
   = help: `at_ext` is the sensor that confirms the cylinder is extended
   = 日本語: パラメータ `at_ext` には bool 型の入力が必要ですが、`conveyor` は出力です
```

**Fix:** Valve parameters take bool outputs; sensor parameters take bool inputs.

### T0405

**unknown device action or state.** A device action or state that does not exist, including mixing them up (`clamp.extend` where `clamp.extended` is meant).

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0405_unknown_action.tejun`:

```text
error[T0405]: Cylinder has no action `extnd`
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0405_unknown_action.tejun:19:27
   |
19 |     state Clamp   { clamp.extnd within 2 s else fault CLAMP_TIMEOUT; -> Press }
   |                           ^^^^^ unknown action
   |
   = help: did you mean `extend`?
   = 日本語: Cylinder に動作 `extnd` はありません
```

**Fix:** Actions are `extend`/`retract`; states are `extended`/`retracted`.

### T0406

**output driven from two places.** An output driven from two places: switched directly while a device drives it, or wired to two device parameters. In ladder logic this is the double coil (二重コイル).

From `tests/fixtures/errors/T0406_double_coil.tejun`:

```text
error[T0406]: `clamp_out` is driven by device `clamp`; switching it directly drives it from two places (double coil)
  --> tests/fixtures/errors/T0406_double_coil.tejun:19:21
   |
19 |     state Clamp   { clamp_out on; clamp.extend within 2 s else fault CLAMP_TIMEOUT; -> Press }
   |                     ^^^^^^^^^ driven by `clamp`
   |
   = help: use `clamp.extend within … else fault …` instead
   = 日本語: `clamp_out` はデバイス `clamp` が駆動しています。直接ONにすると2か所から駆動されます (二重コイル)
```

**Fix:** Let the device drive it (`clamp.extend …`), or wire a separate output.
